nodes.name: Subgroup H_0 via Lemma 1(ii)
nodes.statement: We may assume that $P_0=A_0\cup B_0$. Since $|A_0|+|B_0|=|P_0|$ and $2\cdot C_1\subset P_0\setminus (A_0+B_0)$, it follows from Lemma \ref{lem:ph}~(ii) that there is a proper subgroup $H_0$ of $P_0$ such that $2\cdot C_1$ is contained in a single coset of $H_0$, and that both $A_0$ and $B_0$ are $H_0$--periodic. nodes.name: Odd parts coincide

nodes.name: H'_0 proper via Theorem 1
nodes.statement: It follows that $H'_0$ is a proper subgroup of $L$ since otherwise we get the rainbow--free $3$--coloring $\{ A/L, B/L, C/L\}$ of the cyclic group $G/L$ of order $2^m$, contradicting Theorem \ref{thm:m=0}.

Observe that $H$ contains $A_0$ since $2\cdot A_0\subset H_1\le H$ and the two subgroups $H_1$ and $H$ have the same odd factor. nodes.name: Case 1.2: P_0 trichromatic
nodes.statement: {\it Case 1.2\/}: $P_0$ is trichromatic. nodes.name: Apply induction hypothesis
nodes.statement: By the induction hypothesis there is a subgroup $$H_0=H'_0\oplus \mbox{${\mathbb Z}$}/2^{m-1}\mbox{${\mathbb Z}$},$$ such that $A\subseteq H_0$ and $B_0\setminus H_0$ and $C_0\setminus H_0$ are $H_0$--periodic. nodes.name: Periodicity of B_1, C_1

nodes.name: Conclude Case 1.2
nodes.statement: If $C=G\setminus H$ the statement holds with $H$ and we are done. Since the coloring is rainbow--free, every color $X$ satisfies $2\cdot X\subset X\cup \{ 0\}$. This implies that each of $B\setminus H$ and $C\setminus H$ are not only $H_0$--periodic but in fact $H$--periodic. This concludes this case.
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise the quotient coloring has $A'=\{0\}$, so classes are $H$-periodic outside $H$.

nodes.name: Case 2: both cosets trichromatic
nodes.statement: {\it Case 2\/}: Both cosets of $P_0$ are trichromatic. By the induction hypothesis there is a subgroup $$H_0=H'_0\oplus \mbox{${\mathbb Z}$}/2^{m-1}\mbox{${\mathbb Z}$}$$ of $P_0$ such that $A_0$ is contained in a single coset $H_0$ and $B_0\setminus H_0$ and $C_0\setminus H_0$ are $H_0$--periodic. Choose a minimal $H'_0$ with this property. It follows from Lemma \ref{lem:Kjust} that there is a proper subgroup $$T_0=T'_0\oplus \mbox{${\mathbb Z}$}/2^{m-1}\mbox{${\mathbb Z}$}<P_0$$ containing $H_0$ such that $B_0+C_0\supset P_0\setminus T_0$ and each of $B_0\setminus T_0$ and $C_0\setminus T_0$ is $T_0$--periodic. It follows that $A_1\subset H$ with $$H=T_0'\oplus \mbox{${\mathbb Z}$}/2^m\mbox{${\mathbb Z}$}.$$ Thus $$A\subset H.$$ We now use a similar argument to Case 1.2. For each $x\in L\setminus T_0$ the coset $X=T_0+(2x,0)\subset P_0\setminus T_0$ is monochromatic and, since the coloring is rainbow--free, so that $X= A_0+X$ is disjoint from $T_0+(2x,1)$, the coset $T_0+(x,1)$ is also monochromatic. Hence each of $B_1\setminus (T_0+A_1)$ and $C_1\setminus (T_0+A_1)$ is also $T_0$--periodic. Hence, either $G\setminus H$ is monochromatic and we are done, or $\{ A/H, B/H, C/H\}$ is a rainbow--free $3$--coloring of $G/H$ with the color class $A'=A/H$ consisting only of zero. Hence, every color $X$ satisfies $2\cdot X\subset X\cup \{0\}$. This implies that each of $B\setminus H$ and $C\setminus H$ are not only $T_0$--periodic but in fact $H$--periodic. This completes the proof. \hfill$\Box$
nodes.statement_short: Both cosets of $P_0$ trichromatic.

nodes.name: Apply induction hypothesis
nodes.statement: By the induction hypothesis there is a subgroup $$H_0=H'_0\oplus \mbox{${\mathbb Z}$}/2^{m-1}\mbox{${\mathbb Z}$}$$ of $P_0$ such that $A_0$ is contained in a single coset $H_0$ and $B_0\setminus H_0$ and $C_0\setminus H_0$ are $H_0$--periodic. Choose a minimal $H'_0$ with this property.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $P_0$ gives $H_0$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 12
nodes.statement: It follows from Lemma \ref{lem:Kjust} that there is a proper subgroup $$T_0=T'_0\oplus \mbox{${\mathbb Z}$}/2^{m-1}\mbox{${\mathbb Z}$}<P_0$$ containing $H_0$ such that $B_0+C_0\supset P_0\setminus T_0$ and each of $B_0\setminus T_0$ and $C_0\setminus T_0$ is $T_0$--periodic.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 12 gives $T_0\supseteq H_0$ with $B_0+C_0\supset P_0\setminus T_0$.

nodes.name: A inside H
nodes.statement: We have $$2\cdot A_1\subset P_0\setminus (B_0+C_0),$$ so that $2\cdot A_1\subset T_0$. It follows that $A_1\subset H$ with $$H=T_0'\oplus \mbox{${\mathbb Z}$}/2^m\mbox{${\mathbb Z}$}.$$ Thus $$A\subset H.$$
nodes.statement_short: $2\cdot A_1\subset T_0$, so $A\subset H=T'_0\oplus\mathbb Z/2^m$.

nodes.name: Periodicity outside T_0
nodes.statement: We now use a similar argument to Case 1.2. For each $x\in L\setminus T_0$ the coset $X=T_0+(2x,0)\subset P_0\setminus T_0$ is monochromatic and, since the coloring is rainbow--free, so that $X= A_0+X$ is disjoint from $T_0+(2x,1)$, the coset $T_0+(x,1)$ is also monochromatic. Hence each of $B_1\setminus (T_0+A_1)$ and $C_1\setminus (T_0+A_1)$ is also $T_0$--periodic.
nodes.statement_short: As in Case 1.2, $B_1,C_1$ are $T_0$-periodic off $T_0+A_1$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence, either $G\setminus H$ is monochromatic and we are done, or $\{ A/H, B/H, C/H\}$ is a rainbow--free $3$--coloring of $G/H$ with the color class $A'=A/H$ consisting only of zero. Hence, every color $X$ satisfies $2\cdot X\subset X\cup \{0\}$. This implies that each of $B\setminus H$ and $C\setminus H$ are not only $T_0$--periodic but in fact $H$--periodic. This completes the proof. \hfill$\Box$
nodes.statement_short: Either $G\setminus H$ is monochromatic, or the quotient argument makes $B,C$ $H$-periodic outside $H$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2 (by analogy with Corollary 1)
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{thm:mainodd} provides a proof of Conjecture \ref{cjt}. The proof is completely analogous to the one in Corollary \ref{cor:cjt} for the case of abelian groups of odd order except that we invoke Theorem \ref{thm:mainodd} instead of Theorem \ref{thm:main}.
nodes.statement_short: Same argument as for Corollary 1, with Theorem 7 in place of Theorem 3.

nodes.name: Conjecture 1 for cyclic groups
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be cyclic group of order $n$. Let $p$ denote the smallest odd prime factor of $n$ in ${\mathcal P}_0$ and let $q$ be the smallest odd prime factor of $n$ in ${\mathcal P}_1$. If $\{A,B,C\}$ is a rainbow--free $3$--coloring of $G$ then \begin{equation}\min\{|A|,|B|,|C|\}\leq \left\lfloor \frac{n}{\min \{2p,q\}}\right\rfloor.\end{equation} Moreover, there are rainbow--free $3$--colorings of $G$ for which equality holds.
nodes.statement_short: For every cyclic group Z/nZ the smallest class of a rainbow-free 3-coloring has at most floor(n/min{2p,q}) elements, with equality attainable.
